basics.name: Robotics competition mechanism wikis: Game Manual 0 (gm0, FTC), FRCDesign.org (FRC), and the Unofficial FRC Mechanism Encyclopedia (Project Bucephalus, FRC team 5985)
basics.url: gm0: https://gm0.org/en/latest/ (source repo https://github.com/gamemanual0/gm0). FRCDesign.org: https://frcdesign.org/ (mechanism examples https://frcdesign.org/mechanism-examples/, design handbook https://frcdesign.org/design-handbook/; source repo https://github.com/frcdesign/FRCDesign.org). Mechanism Encyclopedia: https://www.projectb.net.au/resources/robot-mechanisms/ (announced at https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/the-unofficial-frc-mechanism-encyclopedia/398617)
basics.resource_type: encyclopedia/wiki (gm0 and FRCDesign.org are open-source documentation websites built from GitHub repos; the Mechanism Encyclopedia is a single web page of YouTube playlists)
basics.license: gm0: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 2.0 Generic (CC BY-NC 2.0), stated on its License page and in the repo LICENSE, so text and images can be reused non-commercially with credit. FRCDesign.org: calls itself open source, but no LICENSE file was found at the repo root and no licence notice on the pages, so treat it as all rights reserved: link only [uncertain]. Mechanism Encyclopedia: '(c) 2026 Project Bucephalus' footer, no open licence; the videos belong to their YouTube uploaders: link only
basics.language: English (the Mechanism Encyclopedia also offers Portuguese, Turkish, Spanish, Hebrew and French versions)
basics.year: gm0: version 0.2.0 released 14 September 2020 (earlier versions existed) and still updated, with its robot gallery including 2023 to 2025 seasons. FRCDesign.org: publicly launched 31 August 2024, with a 2025-2026 season update thread (August 2025, posts to May 2026). Mechanism Encyclopedia: posted 3 January 2022, updated since (mentions 2022-23 games; footer 2026)
basics.access_barrier: none for reading; FRCDesign's learning course exercises need a free Onshape account, and its FRCDesignLib part library needs a free access form
basics.image_license: gm0: images are photos and CAD renders from FTC teams, presumably under the site's CC BY-NC 2.0 [uncertain]. FRCDesign.org: team photos and CAD screenshots, no licence stated [uncertain]. Mechanism Encyclopedia: embedded or linked YouTube videos under each uploader's terms; small game-piece images credited to FIRST, AndyMark and VEX
basics.authority_level: community (written by experienced FTC/FRC students and mentors, including championship-level teams; not official FIRST documents and not peer reviewed)

coverage.covers: gm0 'Common Mechanisms' (about 35 pages of a roughly 130-page site that also covers team management, electronics and software): design tradeoffs; drivetrains (tank/skid-steer, holonomic, sample drivetrains); power transmission (motion mounting, shaft retention, direct drive, gears, roller chain, timing belt, glossary); linear motion (drawer slides, extrusion slides, linear bearing slides, custom slides, lead screws, rack and pinion, rigging); arms; linkages (linkage slides, four-bar, virtual four-bar); passive intake/claw; active intake (roller, wheeled, compliant wheel); transfers; dead wheels (odometry); full and mini turrets; plus motor gearbox internals (spur vs planetary), servo guide, fastener guide and 3D printing/machining/laser cutting guides. FRCDesign.org (169 pages, 114 of them in the Onshape learning course): design handbook on structure, materials, fasteners, 3D printing and motion components (flanged, standard, needle and X-contact bearings, bushings, hex and round axles); course projects on belts, chain, gears, shafts and bearings, motors, backlash, chain tensioning, compression, 'zombie axles', cable clamps, chain attachment, elevator bearing blocks and rigging; mechanism examples in 5 families (swerve drivebases, pivoting and linkage intakes, shooters, continuous and cascade elevators, pivots) with 3 in-depth write-ups. Mechanism Encyclopedia: about 44 YouTube playlists in 8 sections (game piece examples, 8 drivetrain types, 10 intake playlists by game piece, 5 indexers, 4 lift types, 7 shooter types, 5 climber types, 4 miscellaneous such as turrets and suction)
coverage.organisation: By robot function (subsystem): drivetrain, intake, lift/linear motion, arm, shooter, climber, turret, power transmission. The Mechanism Encyclopedia adds a second key: the kind of object to be handled (small balls, large balls, cubes, rings, cones, poles), which lets a beginner look up by 'what do I need to pick up' without knowing any terms. gm0 and FRCDesign use sidebar trees and search. This works well for robot builders but not for someone looking for a joint or connection type
coverage.scope_match: low to medium: mostly whole robot subsystems (drivetrains, shooters, intakes, climbers), which the project treats as whole machines, plus standard hardware; but they do cover in-scope transmission and motion types (planetary vs spur gearboxes, chain, belt, rack and pinion, lead screws, cascade vs continuous rigging, four-bar and virtual four-bar, over-centre linkages, shaft retention methods, bearings and bushings) at a practical maker level
coverage.taxonomy_used: By subsystem/function. gm0 'Common Mechanisms' has 11 groups (design tradeoffs, drivetrains, power transmission, linear motion, arms, linkages, passive intake/claw, active intake, transfers, dead wheels, turrets). FRCDesign mechanism examples have 5 groups (drivebases, intakes, shooters, elevators, pivots). The Mechanism Encyclopedia has 7 mechanism sections (drivetrains, intakes, indexers, lifts, shooters, climbers, others), sub-sorted by game piece or by type
coverage.example_types: Virtual four-bar (belt- or chain-linked arm that keeps the end level); four-bar linkage; linkage-driven slides; over-centre linkage to resist back-driving; cascade vs continuous elevator rigging; drawer-slide and extrusion-slide linear extensions; lead screw; rack and pinion; planetary vs spur gearbox; bevel gears; roller chain and timing belt (GT2/HTD) drives with idlers and turnbuckle tensioners; dead axle vs live axle vs 'zombie axle'; hex-shaft interfaces; set-screw vs clamping shaft collars and E-clip retaining rings; X-contact (four-point) bearing; needle bearing press-fitted into a roller end cap; crush blocks in box tube; compliant intake wheels; suction/vacuum grippers; turrets; mecanum, swerve, H-drive and kiwi drives
coverage.making_methods: Competition robotics (FTC kit systems such as goBILDA and REV; FRC aluminium box tube, COTS parts), with 3D printing (PLA, PETG, TPU and more), CNC machining, laser cutting and Onshape CAD
coverage.item_count: gm0: about 130 pages in total, about 35 of them on mechanisms. FRCDesign.org: 169 pages (114 learning course, 7 design handbook, about 12 mechanism example pages). Mechanism Encyclopedia: about 44 YouTube playlists, each holding many videos
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Over-centre: yes (gm0 linkages page: driving a linkage over centre makes it harder to back-drive). Self-locking: partly (back-drive resistance of over-centre linkages; lead screws) [uncertain]. Gear trains/gearboxes: yes, strongly (spur vs planetary gearboxes with shock-load advice, gear ratios, bevel gears, chain and belt reductions, backlash sources and fixes). Torque-limiting, one-way/ratchet, indexing/detent, hand-release only: not found in the pages read [uncertain]. Compliant: only compliant (soft rubber) intake wheels, not compliant mechanisms. Print-in-place: no. Powered connectors: motors and servos as actuators only; no electromagnets or solenoid latches found [uncertain]. Adhesives: only thread-locking compound on shaft-retention bolts; no adhesive types
coverage.entry_structure: gm0: page per mechanism with plain description, highlighted 'Term' definitions, advantages and disadvantages, tips and warnings, photos of real team robots, and sometimes an interactive Onshape CAD example. FRCDesign.org: handbook pages with tables and photos; mechanism examples with links (CAD document, Chief Delphi build thread) and a 'Behind the Design' write-up of the reasoning (torque analysis, gearbox packaging); course pages with exercises. Mechanism Encyclopedia: table rows of type, short notes and a playlist link
coverage.audience_level: competition robotics (high-school FTC/FRC students and mentors; hobbyist-friendly)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: high: written for rookie teams in plain language, with glossaries (gm0 'Know Your Lingo' and per-section glossaries; FRCDesign glossary) and lots of photos; some FTC/FRC slang and vendor names (goBILDA, REV, WCP, SDS) need decoding
usefulness.has_images: yes: many photos of real competition robots and CAD renders (e.g. 19 images on gm0's rigging page, 20 on FRCDesign's motion components page), generally good quality
usefulness.has_animations: yes, video: the Mechanism Encyclopedia is entirely YouTube playlists of robots in action; gm0 embeds some YouTube videos (e.g. on over-centre linkages) and links interactive Onshape CAD models you can drag to see motion; FRCDesign links public Onshape CAD documents
usefulness.gaps: Aimed at complete robot subsystems in a competition context, not at connection types; little on joints, latches, clutches, snap fits, print-in-place, adhesives or powered latches; heavy reliance on vendor-specific kit parts (goBILDA, REV, WCP); no index by behaviour (locks, slips, one-way); the Encyclopedia gives no explanations beyond one-paragraph notes
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes for gm0 and FRCDesign: stable per-topic URLs good for 'see a real example' links, e.g. https://gm0.org/en/latest/docs/common-mechanisms/linkages.html (four-bar, virtual four-bar, over-centre), https://gm0.org/en/latest/docs/common-mechanisms/power-transmission/shaft-retention.html, https://gm0.org/en/latest/docs/common-mechanisms/linear-motion-guide/rigging.html, https://frcdesign.org/design-handbook/power-transmission/motion-components/. gm0 uses a 'latest' version path, which is stable but may shift if pages are renamed. The Encyclopedia has only one page with anchor sections
usefulness.reusable_data: gm0: structured source (reStructuredText in a public GitHub repo, Sphinx build) under CC BY-NC 2.0, so the list and text can be reused non-commercially with credit. FRCDesign.org: public GitHub repo (Astro/Starlight MDX pages, a glossary data folder) and a sitemap, but no licence found, so link only [uncertain]. Mechanism Encyclopedia: scrape-only single page, all rights reserved
usefulness.maintained: yes: gm0 is live on Read the Docs with a CI and link-check workflow, gallery updated to 2025; FRCDesign.org is actively developed (Stage 1A rework, Stage 2 rework, FRCDesignLib and FRCDesignApp in 2025-2026); the Mechanism Encyclopedia page is online with a 2026 footer, and the author promised continuous playlist updates
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Look up by the object or job, not by the term: the Encyclopedia's 'what game piece do you need to grab' key maps well to a flow-chart question such as 'what are you holding or moving?'. (2) gm0's Design Tradeoffs table (problem vs solution with short pros and cons) as a compact comparison format. (3) Highlighted 'Term' boxes that define the proper name inline, matching the project's plain-English-first style. (4) FRCDesign's 'Behind the Design' write-ups that explain why a real design chose a mechanism. (5) Link an interactive CAD model you can drag, or a playlist of real examples, from each entry. (6) Advantages/disadvantages lists and 'Danger/Tip' call-outs per type
usefulness.design_rules_given: some: gm0 gives gear centre-distance and pitch-diameter formulas, gear mesh advice, filament temperatures, and reach targets (more than 18 in extension, 24 in preferred); FRCDesign gives 3D-printing clearance of about 0.1 to 0.5 mm (0.004 to 0.020 in) depending on fit, teardrop holes (100 degrees), bolt sizes with tap and close-fit drill sizes, and keep gear reductions to 3 stages or fewer to limit backlash; the Encyclopedia gives none
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: FRCDesign's FRCDesignLib (a shared Onshape library of configurable parts such as spacers, crush blocks and HTD pulleys), FeatureScripts and KrayonCAD for quick robot layouts; gm0 links example Onshape documents; the Encyclopedia has none
usefulness.file_formats: Web pages; Onshape CAD documents (viewable in a browser, exportable to STEP/STL through Onshape); YouTube video; gm0 can be built to PDF from its source (make latexpdf)
usefulness.terminology_value: medium: good for maker/competition names and slang (virtual four-bar, cascade vs continuous rigging, dead/live/zombie axle, crush block, over the bumper intake, C2C centre-to-centre) with definitions, but these are community terms, not formal engineering names, and there are no translations except the Encyclopedia's page languages
usefulness.decision_support: gm0 Design Tradeoffs table comparing common choices (2 vs 4 drive motors, claw vs intake, spur vs planetary gearbox, arm vs linear extension) with short reasons and recommendations; FRCDesign 'intake golden rules' and backlash source/solution tables; the Encyclopedia's two-key table (subsystem by game piece) works as a simple lookup. No interactive selector or flow chart
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: gm0 is the FTC counterpart of FRC resources and links FTC Docs, REV documentation and Spectrum 3847's reading list; FRCDesign.org builds on Onshape learning courses and Chief Delphi / Open Alliance build threads (e.g. 6328, 1678, 2910 robots) and overlaps gm0 on power transmission and linear motion; the Mechanism Encyclopedia curates team reveal videos from YouTube (FRC, FTC, VEX) and was inspired by team 1678's 'steal from the best, invent the rest'
